## Historical audit — S0266

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/results/task02/structured/C1/test/commons_96943062/trajectory.jsonl`. All references below are to this file’s JSONL lines. The supplied observations contain no image pixels accessible for independent comparison.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal: student `model_request`, line 1 | Reconstruct a single 384 × 512 indoor photograph as an editable, multi-mesh SceneAct/Blender scene, matching camera and framing. The student’s inferred scene inventory—not independently verified here—describes a damaged classroom without visible furniture. |
| First build: student `model_response` and `execute`, lines 3–4 | Code creates multiple distinct assets: room, ceiling tiles and openings, board, flag, fittings, debris and rails. It groups board frame, seam and tray; flag and pole; and debris components. These are programmed relationships, not verification of physical connection, support or completeness. Colors, roughness and attempted procedural carpet texture are specified; a camera and two area lights are set. |
| First validation: `execution_result` line 5; `select` line 6; student `model_request` line 7 | Execution succeeded in 13.25 seconds and saved a render and blend file. The subsequent request supplied the reference and render for comparison. This establishes render availability to the student, not independent visual fidelity. |
| Autonomous revision: student `model_response` line 9; `execute` line 10 | The student reported the rear-wall boundary and depth-line convergence as mismatched, the board near edge as too short, the flag as too far back, panels as too large and bright, and insulation as too flat. It then combined camera repositioning, board extension, flag relocation and stripe reorientation, debris pose/depth and material changes, thicker-looking layered insulation, lighting changes and a dedicated procedural carpet material. These are student diagnoses and executed changes, not independently verified defects or causal tests. |
| Final visible result: `execution_result` line 11; `select` line 12 | Step 2 succeeded in 15.00 seconds, saved a render and blend file, and was selected. No later image review, score, or formal task-success judgment is visible. Technical build success is established; photographic and geometric correctness remain **unknown**. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No teacher event, teacher diagnosis, proposed teacher update, or receipt/adoption of teacher advice appears in this student trajectory. The runtime’s post-render instruction requested comparison and a revision if supported (line 7); it is not evidence of a teacher intervention. The student independently produced one combined revision after render feedback; the recorded CLI sessions report no tool calls (lines 2 and 8).

**Uncertainty and lessons.** The code contains multiple objects, named child parts, materials, object poses, camera and lighting, but neither their appearance nor connections are independently inspected here. In particular, whether the ceiling openings, cabinet interior, debris overlaps, carpet texture, framing and illumination match the photograph remains unresolved. The student’s multi-anchor comparison and separate parameter families are transferable review practices; the particular classroom geometry and corrections are task-specific hypotheses. Because several families changed together, the successful second render cannot identify which change helped or whether the reconstruction improved.
